instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Pat the 1.5 lb pork dry and season it all over with 3/4 tsp of the salt and the 1/2 tsp pepper.
Peel and core the apples and cut them into slices about 1/3 inch thick. Chop the 2 shallots, then strip and chop 1 tbsp of the thyme leaves.

Melt 2 tbsp of the butter in a large ovenproof skillet over medium high. Add the apples and sprinkle the 1 tsp sugar over them. Cook for 6 to 8 minutes, turning them now and then, until they're golden brown on both sides. Tip them onto a plate.
Wipe out the skillet with a paper towel and melt 2 more tbsp butter in it over medium high. Add the pork and sear it for about 2 minutes a side, turning it until it's golden brown all over.

Put the skillet in the oven and roast the pork for 10 to 15 minutes. You're cooking it to 145°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check it at the thickest part. No thermometer? Cut into the thickest part: it's done when the center is a light blush pink and the juices run clear.
Take the skillet out with an oven mitt. Move the pork to a board and cover it loosely with foil to rest. Keep the mitt on the handle while you make the sauce. It stays hot for a long time.
Set the skillet over medium and melt the last 1 tbsp butter in it. Add the shallots and the thyme and cook for 2 minutes, stirring, until the shallots are soft.
Pour in the 1/4 cup Calvados and let it boil for about a minute, scraping up the browned bits, until it's down to a sticky glaze. Stand back a little. It can flare up.
Stir in the 1 cup cream and the 1/4 cup cider. Boil for about 3 minutes, stirring, until the sauce is thick enough to coat a spoon.
Add the apples and any juices from under the pork and warm them through for 1 minute. Taste the sauce, and stir in the last 1/4 tsp salt if it's flat.
Slice the pork about 1/2 inch thick and serve it with the apples and sauce spooned over.
method_notes: All three brown apples in butter, cook the pork, then build the sauce in the same pan with apple, cider and cream. What A Girl Eats (from a Bon Appétit recipe) sears a tenderloin, finishes it in a 375°F oven to 145°F, and makes the sauce with shallot, thyme, Calvados, cream and a little cider. The French Cooking Academy pan fries chops slowly in butter, deglazes with dry cider and adds Calvados at the end; Krumpli braises thick chops with bacon, brandy, cider, stock and crème fraîche. No version had 20 or more ratings and RecipeTin Eats (the trusted cook for French) has no version, so the first read version leads. This one roasts the pork in the same skillet so it all stays in one pan.
